sections.h2: Where and how do Muhlenberg County owners pay the Sheriff?
sections.html:
Payment happens at the Sheriff's Office inside the courthouse at 100 South Main Street, Greenville, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. The number is 270-338-3345, and the mailing address is PO Box 227, Greenville, KY 42345.

  • Bills normally go out October 30, and collection opens November 1.
  • Online payment is possible. Telephone payment is not.
  • A drop box behind the courthouse, near the elevator entrance, accepts payments outside office hours.
  • Only full payment is taken, so a part payment does not count.

Value is a different question and belongs to the county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). The sheriff's own site says assessed values may change before they are final.

sections.h2: What shaped Muhlenberg County, and what does it mean for a sale?
sections.html:
The county covers 479 square miles of western Kentucky, 467 of them land. The Green River and Lake Malone are its two main waters. Greenville is the seat, and Central City is the largest community. Logan and Christian counties gave up the land in 1798.

Coal built the local economy. Kentucky's first commercial coal mine opened here in 1820 along the Green River at Paradise, and during most of the 1970s no other county in the country mined more. Surface coal has been stripped out, and what remains lies deep. The north is gentle hill country with river flats and bald cypress swamps along Cypress Creek. The south has higher relief, gorges and sandstone outcrops. Lake Malone State Park, with a 788-acre lake, sits near Dunmor.

Listings therefore range widely, from town lots in Greenville and Central City to ground near the lake and parcels in old mining country. One public school system operates under the Muhlenberg County Board of Education, and a single Muhlenberg County High School has served the county since June 2009.

sections.h2: How do Muhlenberg County Census figures read for housing?
sections.html:
The population estimate for July 2025 is 30,634, which is 1.0% below the 2020 base, and 21.3% of residents are past 65. Home prices are modest, and so are tax bills.

  • 13,640 housing units in 2025, with just 5 building permits that year.
  • Owners occupy 78.8% of homes during 2020 to 2024.
  • The Census midpoint for an owned house is $127,400.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,167 with a mortgage and $396 without.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $718.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $51,927, and 19.1% of people are in poverty.

About 88.7% of residents did not move in the prior year. With so few new permits, a buyer here mostly picks among houses that already exist.

sections.h2: Which Muhlenberg County economy details matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Buyers ask about jobs, schools and commuting. Coal mining in the county and its neighbors began to grow again as the 2000s opened. The Greater Muhlenberg Chamber of Commerce, created in January 2006 when the Central City and Greenville chambers merged, counted over 155 member businesses at the time.

The Census Bureau lists 537 employer establishments for 2023, and employment rose 6.7% between 2022 and 2023. Retail sales for 2022 were $374,858 thousand, or $12,212 per resident. Workers spend a mean of 27.0 minutes getting to their jobs. The schools consolidated in steps, from eight secondary schools to two high schools in 1990 and then to one. A sheriff's receipt showing the year's bill paid is the quickest answer to a buyer's first question about taxes.

sections.h2: What else about Muhlenberg County do buyers and heirs ask?
sections.html:
Many calls come from heirs, so some numbers help. The Census Bureau counts 1,758 veterans in the county, and 16.5% of residents under 65 live with a disability. Some 84.2% of households have a broadband subscription, and 14.7% of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Health care and social assistance brought in $144,467 thousand in 2022, and lodging and food service sales were $39,476 thousand.

Culture and services cluster in the two main towns. Central City has a convention center with an outdoor pool and spray park. Muhlenberg County Public Libraries runs the Thistle Cottage Genealogy and History Annex in Greenville, a useful stop for anyone tracing an old deed chain. The county lies at the southern edge of the Evansville, Indiana television market. John Prine's song 'Paradise' criticized strip mining here and refers to the community where the 1820 mine opened.

sections.h2: What are the Muhlenberg County payment windows?
sections.html:
The sheriff's posted dates follow KRS 134.015, with a discount first, the printed amount next and penalties after.

Muhlenberg County Sheriff, month-by-month bill totals
Month paidResult for the owner
Whole of NovemberSubtract 2 percent
Whole of DecemberPay the printed total
Whole of JanuaryAdd 5 percent
February 1 through April 15Add 21 percent

Whatever the month, the sheriff wants the entire bill in one payment. On a $1,200 bill the figures are $1,176 in November, $1,200 in December, $1,260 in January and $1,452 from February through April 15. Waiting the full season costs $276 more than paying early.

After April 15 the county clerk handles delinquent bills, so a seller with an old unpaid year should call the clerk for the payoff.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Muhlenberg County valuation?
sections.html:
The PVA sets value as of January 1. Under KRS 133.120, the owner first meets the PVA or a deputy during the tax roll's 13-day public inspection in May, which KRS 133.045 schedules. Anyone still dissatisfied files a written petition with the County Clerk naming the parcel, the reasons and the value the owner proposes, within a workday after the inspection ends.

The appeals board will deny a case if the owner refuses to supply reasonable value information the PVA or board requests, so assemble sales comparisons, an appraisal or repair estimates early. Nothing about a filed appeal postpones the due date, because the bill stays payable on the normal schedule while the case proceeds. A taxpayer who never appears before the county board cannot reach the state Board of Tax Appeals afterward. Tax is paid on the owner's claimed value, with any increase billed later plus interest.

sections.h2: What exemption is available to older Muhlenberg County owners?
sections.html: Owners 65 and up, and those totally disabled, can subtract $49,100 from assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. Applied to the county midpoint of $127,400, that leaves $78,300 subject to tax. The Muhlenberg County PVA takes the application along with proof of age: a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability filers renew annually unless they are service-connected veterans or have been ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What should a Muhlenberg County seller settle before the deed is signed?
sections.html:
The tax is a personal obligation of whoever owned the property on January 1. A delinquent bill places a lien on the parcel for up to eleven years under KRS 134.420, regardless of owner.

  • Ask the sheriff whether this year's bill has been paid and in which window.
  • Put the proration in writing in the sales contract.
  • Enter the buyer's address for future bills on the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • When a deceased owner's heirs sell, the executor first files an affidavit with the county clerk naming recipients and values.

faqs.q: Is telephone payment accepted by the Muhlenberg County Sheriff?
faqs.a: No. The office takes payment online, by mail to PO Box 227, in person at 100 South Main Street, or in the courthouse drop box.

faqs.q: May an owner send part of a Muhlenberg County bill?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's FAQ requires payment in full.

faqs.q: How long is the Muhlenberg County discount window?
faqs.a: All of November. The printed amount is due in December, and the penalty starts January 1.

faqs.q: What hours does the Muhlenberg County Sheriff keep?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., at 100 South Main Street in Greenville. The phone is 270-338-3345.

faqs.q: What is the Muhlenberg County deduction for seniors?
faqs.a: The state subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026 once an owner 65 or older, or totally disabled, applies at the PVA.
